walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Members of a homologous series share:
options: The same molecular mass
The same functional group and general formula
The same boiling point
The same number of isomers

mcqs.q: What does Kp use instead of concentrations?
options: Kp uses the volumes of each gas in the mixture.
A buffer destroys added acid by changing it into water vapour.
Kp uses the total pressure of the system raised to the stoichiometric coefficients.
Partial pressures of each gaseous component at equilibrium.

mcqs.q: What does an NMR chemical shift (δ, in ppm) actually measure?
options: Chemical shift is the absolute resonance frequency of the nucleus in Hz.
Kp uses the volumes of each gas in the mixture.
The position of a peak RELATIVE to TMS (tetramethylsilane, δ = 0), normalised by the spectrometer frequency.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.

mcqs.q: How does a buffer maintain its pH when small amounts of acid are added?
options: A buffer prevents any H+ ions from being added to the solution at all.
Kp uses the volumes of each gas in the mixture.
A buffer destroys added acid by changing it into water vapour.
The conjugate base in the buffer reacts with added H+ to remove it, keeping pH nearly constant.
